preview.author: Ben Olawumi

pick.text: There’s little to play for but pride here, meaning both sides could play with the freedom to make both teams to score in both halves more viable than in normal circumstances.

preview.synopsis: Cyprus have little left to play for; Montenegro are unbeaten in six H2Hs. The writer leans to both teams scoring in both halves because of the relaxed stakes.

strengths.home: Unbeaten in the cycle since the opening 2-1 loss in Montenegro, 3 straight home wins, 2nd place and March play-off already secured. Few goals recently (3 of last 9 over 2.5). Pileas back from suspension.
strengths.away: Beat Latvia 2-1 with a 91st-minute winner to top Group C2; Osmajic is in form (8 goals in 12). Both teams scored in 5 of last 6. Savic suspended, Loncar returns.

preview.author: Tom Penn

pick.text: Given Latvia’s miserable form and Armenia’s poor away results over the last two years, backing a draw could be the way to go.

preview.synopsis: A dead-rubber with Latvia in poor form and Armenia poor on the road. The writer suggests the draw.

strengths.home: Bottom of the group with one point all cycle and a 7-game winless run (D1, L6); has scored first in only one UNL group game. Their best results came at home.
strengths.away: Rescued a 1-1 draw with Cyprus but cannot progress; weak away form (no goal in 4 of last 5 away) and leaky before half-time. Gharibyan in good scoring form.

preview.author: Aaron Murphy

pick.text: The high stakes of the match and sound defending of both teams make under 2.5 goals seem a tempting angle.

preview.synopsis: High stakes and two sound defences. The writer likes under 2.5 goals.

strengths.home: One of League C's best defences: 4 straight clean sheets, 6 in last 10; needs a win for League B. Kontsevoy has 8 goals in 8 games; both Shumansky and Barkouski back from bans.
strengths.away: Group leaders, won the reverse 2-0 and 4 of the last 5 meetings. Manaj has 13 goals for club and country this season; near full strength. Rarely win by 2+ (5 of last 17).

preview.author: Matt Jones

pick.text: San Marino just cannot keep the back door closed and have already crumbled against Finland once this season, so value may be found here in backing Finland to overcome a -2 handicap.

preview.synopsis: Heavy home favourites after a 7-0 reverse. The writer backs Finland to overcome a -2 handicap.

strengths.home: Lost only one of last six at home (W4, D1), 4 clean sheets in 5 home games, 11+ shots in 5 of last 6; Tenho and Markhiev suspended. Won the 7 previous H2Hs 30-2.
strengths.away: Lost all five UNL games, conceding a competition-high 18 goals; 18 straight defeats. Capicchioni foul-prone; Fabbri suspended.

preview.author: John Pennington

pick.text: Belgium’s inconsistency during this campaign and Italy’s excellent recent record on the road suggests it might be worth considering backing the draw.

preview.synopsis: Belgium need a win, Italy only a draw. The writer points to the draw because of Belgium's inconsistency and Italy's strong away record.

strengths.home: Alternating wins and defeats lately (W4, L3) but strong at home (one home loss since Nov 2024), 5 clean sheets in 7 home games; De Ketelaere in form, Lukaku doubtful.
strengths.away: Top of the group after beating France 3-1; just need to avoid defeat. Conceded once in each of last four, only 5 of last 6 away games went under 2.5 goals. No new injuries.

preview.author: Tomáš Vlasák

pick.text: Croatia’s dominant head-to-head record is hard to ignore, making a home win a very appealing play here.

preview.synopsis: Croatia's H2H record and home form against a winless Czech side. The writer picks a Croatia win.

strengths.home: Unbeaten in 7 H2Hs (W4, D3), won 8 of last 11 competitive home games (5 of last 7 by 2+). But a group-high 16 conceded and four defeats this UNL, including 7-0 vs England.
strengths.away: Lost all five UNL games and scored twice; no clean sheet in 12 matches. Captain Krejci suspended; Subert and Provod left the squad ill.

preview.author: Chris Wilson

pick.text: Turkey’s form in this cycle and tendency to start slowly point towards France/France in the half-time/full-time market being a solid choice.

preview.synopsis: France need a point; Turkey tend to start slowly. The writer chooses France to lead at half-time and win, via the half-time/full-time market.

strengths.home: Unbeaten in 9 UNL group games before losing to Italy; no competitive home defeat since Sept 2024; 10 of 13 goals this cycle after half-time. Need only avoid defeat. Mbappe hoped back.
strengths.away: Bottom of the group; seven goals conceded before the half-hour mark and behind at half-time in four of last five. Kabak suspended; Cakir very busy in goal.

preview.author: Ryan Fisher

pick.text: Given recent H2H meetings, both teams to score and over 2.5 goals looks a fairly safe avenue to explore.

preview.synopsis: A group-deciding clash; each of the last five H2Hs saw both teams score and 3+ goals. The writer favours both teams to score and over 2.5 goals.

strengths.home: 100% record in this cycle, 43 games unbeaten in 90 minutes, no home defeat under de la Fuente; Yamal, Laporte, N. Williams and Oyarzabal expected back.
strengths.away: Beat Croatia 2-1 and still in contention to top the group; won the reverse 3-2. Bellingham has contributed to 14 goals in 13 games; no fresh injury issues.
